verdicts.reasoning: The short form 'Order on Motion for Extension of Time to File Response/Reply AND Set/Reset Deadlines' matches the long form on every point. (1) Both are orders: the long form is a minute order. (2) Both act on the same kind of motion: the long form grants the 103 Motion for Extension of Time, and the window shows #103 (463453160) is an 'Unopposed MOTION for Extension of Time to File Response/Reply as to 77 MOTION to Dismiss' by the Federal Defendants. (3) Both reset a deadline: the long form extends the Federal Defendants' reply deadline to May 29, 2026, which is the Set/Reset Deadlines event. (4) Same day: both are dated May 8. The short form's time_filed is 16:04 ET, after #103 was filed at 14:38 ET, which fits an order signed 5/8/2026. The short form names nothing the long form does not do. Nothing else in the window fits it. The only other long-form order is 463276981, a May 7 order on the 102 Motion to Withdraw, and it already has its own short form (463283251, 'Order on Motion to Withdraw as Attorney'). #103 and #104 are filings, not orders. 468293503 is another, less specific short form of the same type, not a separate long-form entry.

The short form 'Order on Motion for Extension of Time to File Response/Reply' fits the long form fully. Both are orders on a motion of that type: the long form grants #103, which the window shows is a 'MOTION for Extension of Time to File Response/Reply'. Both are dated May 8, and the short form names nothing the long form does not do. The short form gives no motion number, party or deadline, so the pair rests on type alone. To rule out the case where it belongs to a different same-day order, I checked the window. It has only one extension motion (#103) and only one long-form order on such a motion dated May 8 (463654829). #103 and #104 are filings, and the only other long-form order (463276981) is a May 7 withdrawal order. Caveats for the other lenses: (a) this object was created 2026-06-22, about six weeks after the event, and has no time_filed; (b) it lacks the 'AND Set/Reset Deadlines' event that the earlier short form 463480957 (May 8, 16:04) carries. Leaving out an event does not make it inconsistent, and nothing in the window points to a second extension order that day, so I read it as one more CourtListener record of the same May 8 minute order. 463480957 fits this text as well or better, but it is itself a short-form record of that same order, not a separate minute entry, so I do not name it as a better match.

The window (5/7 to 5/9) holds 7 objects. Only one is an order on a motion for extension of time: the long form 463654829, the MINUTE ORDER granting the 103 Motion for Extension of Time. It extends the reply deadline to May 29, which also covers the 'AND Set/Reset Deadlines' part of the short text. The numbered entries are 103 and 104. Entry 103 is the Unopposed MOTION for Extension of Time itself, filed at 14:38. It is a motion, not an order. Entry 104 is a memorandum in opposition to motion 97. An 'Order on Motion...' text cannot describe either one. The only other minute order, 463276981, grants the 102 Motion to Withdraw on 5/7. It already has its own short form of matching type, 463283251 ('Order on Motion to Withdraw as Attorney'). 468293503 is a second unnumbered short form of the same type, with its description taken from a document. It is not a separate entry with its own docket text, so it is not a different minute entry. The short form's time_filed of 16:04 on 5/8 comes after motion 103 was filed at 14:38, which fits an order granting it the same afternoon. The long form is the only entry in the window this short form can describe.
